title: Empty-donor observation is insufficient to certify productive transfer in the stated reactions
statement: Under the two reaction states specified in the XH1 source, productive transfer from an upstream 3'-O-acylated DNA donor U-O-CO-P_n and hydrolysis both produce the same observed upstream state U-OH. Therefore a downstream sensor that observes only donor emptiness cannot distinguish completion from hydrolysis. This is an exact state-aliasing failure in the listed model, not a statement about the physical frequency of hydrolysis.

requires: The transition alternatives and observable are exactly those stated in the XH1 source.
Only the upstream donor state U-OH is observed; the receiving adaptor or released product is not observed.
provides: A necessary observation-design constraint: donor-empty alone does not certify productive transfer.
The specified ribosomal comparison has a distinct receiving-carrier state: transfer places chain on the next tRNA while hydrolysis leaves it unchanged.
assumptions: The result concerns the listed state transition descriptions; it does not assert that any physical apparatus has large hydrolysis or that an arbitrary chemistry has the same transitions.
costs: No rate, hydrolysis prevalence, sensor performance, or full assembly workflow is supplied.
contract.units: Discrete reaction states; no kinetic units.
contract.obstruction: A product-qualified receiving state or a separately justified hydrolysis bound is required for the intended decision. This does not establish a working sensor or product-gated progression.

evidence.range_scope: Exact donor-empty aliasing and the separate ribosomal receiving-carrier contrast.
evidence.status: Exact selected original bytes; this intake preserves and indexes the passage.
evidence.quote: For upstream 3'-O-acylated DNA donor U–O–CO–P_n, both (1) productive aminoacyl transfer to an aminated downstream adaptor D and (2) hydrolysis to free chain P_n–COOH produce U–OH.

body: The state table is a direct observation-map comparison: both listed transitions agree on donor_empty but disagree on recipient_carries_chain/free_chain. The source's arithmetic-only script encodes this Boolean aliasing but was not executed; the check here is limited to the written two-state logic.

review.scope: Exact indistinguishability of two supplied transition alternatives under the sole empty-donor observation. Product occupancy on the receiving carrier separates this pair, but no reaction rate, physical sensor, chemical identity guarantee or implemented assembler is established.
